name: Apple Pie
summary: A two crust apple pie on plain pastry, after Fannie Farmer's 1896 method.
ingredients: 6 sour apples, pared and sliced thin

equipment.help: A pie wants a hot start to set the bottom crust, and ovens differ in how they give it.
equipment.label: Oven

steps.title: Rub in the fat
steps.body: Cut the cold fat into the flour and salt until the mixture looks like coarse meal.

steps.title: Bring the pastry together
steps.body: Sprinkle in the ice water a spoonful at a time, just until it holds. Do not knead it; a shaggy dough makes a tender crust.

steps.title: Rest the pastry
steps.body: Wrap it and let it rest cold.

steps.title: Roll the bottom crust
steps.body: Roll half the pastry thin and line the pie plate, letting it overhang.

steps.title: Slice the apples
steps.body: Pare, core and slice the apples thin and even, so they cook through together.

steps.title: Fill the pie
steps.body: Mix the apples with the sugar, spice and lemon juice. Heap them in the crust and dot with butter.

steps.title: Put on the top crust
steps.body: Roll the rest of the pastry, lay it over, trim and press the edges, and cut a few slits for steam.

steps.title: Heat a gas oven to 450°F
steps.body: Bake low in a gas oven so the bottom crust sets before the top browns.

steps.title: Heat an electric oven to 450°F
steps.body: A preheated baking sheet on the lower rack helps the bottom crust.

steps.title: Heat a convection oven to 425°F
steps.body: Drop the heat 25°F for the fan and expect it to brown a little sooner.

steps.title: Bake hot, then lower
steps.body: Bake hot for fifteen minutes to set the crust, then lower the oven to 350°F for the rest.

steps.title: Finish baking
steps.body: Bake until the crust is golden and the juice bubbles through the slits.

steps.title: Cool before cutting
steps.body: Let the pie cool so the filling sets. Cutting it hot makes it run.
